item.name: emit CloudWatch EMF metrics with Powertools
item.summary: A private Worker preview runs actual Powertools Metrics, parses generated EMF, and checks configured namespace and dimensions; it makes no AWS calls.

manifest.original_contribution: Original, focused Node.js Lambda integration module for Embedded Metric Format business metrics using the pinned AWS Powertools TypeScript package.

delivery_contract.format: self-contained JSON with exact UTF-8 file contents
delivery_contract.side_effects: The private bounded preview runs only local product behavior and fixtures; buyer deployment may perform AWS service calls as documented.

manifest.supported_boundary: A Node.js Lambda helper for EMF count metrics. Private preview executes actual Powertools Metrics and validates its local EMF namespace and dimensions; no CloudWatch ingestion or AWS call is verified.

Record count metrics with the actual Powertools Metrics implementation and flush them as CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) JSON. CloudWatch extracts EMF asynchronously from the Lambda log stream; this helper does not call `PutMetricData`.

## Install and use

Install `@aws-lambda-powertools/metrics` at exactly 2.36.0 and run in Node.js 20 or newer in Lambda.

```js
import { createMetrics, recordCount, flushMetrics } from './src/metrics.mjs';
const metrics = createMetrics({ namespace: 'Payments', service_name: 'capture' });
export const handler = async (event) => {
  try {
    recordCount(metrics, 'PaymentAccepted');
    return { statusCode: 200 };
  } finally {
    flushMetrics(metrics);
  }
};
```

Use low-cardinality dimensions such as environment or service. Do not put customer IDs, request IDs, or other high-cardinality values in dimensions; use metadata when appropriate. Powertools enforces EMF metric and dimension limits. `publishStoredMetrics()` writes to stdout; it is not proof CloudWatch has ingested the document.

## Native private preview and boundary

The private preview runs the actual Powertools Metrics API, captures its generated EMF JSON, and checks the configured namespace, service and custom dimensions, and count before returning bounded diagnostics. A preview-only `node:console` alias implements only the `Console.log` method that this pinned Metrics path calls and forwards the real generated line to the local output sink. The Worker profile has no CloudWatch ingestion; `local_fixture_only` means no AWS call or service-side success is asserted.

const SERVICE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$/;
const METRIC = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,254}$/;

export function createMetrics({ namespace, service_name, default_dimensions = {} } = {}) {
  if (typeof namespace !== 'string' || !namespace.trim() || namespace.length > 255) throw new Error('invalid_namespace');
  if (typeof service_name !== 'string' || !SERVICE.test(service_name)) throw new Error('invalid_service_name');
  if (!default_dimensions || Array.isArray(default_dimensions) || typeof default_dimensions !== 'object'
      || Object.keys(default_dimensions).length > 8
      || Object.values(default_dimensions).some(value => typeof value !== 'string' || value.length > 250)) {
    throw new Error('invalid_default_dimensions');
  }
  return new Metrics({ namespace, serviceName: service_name, defaultDimensions: default_dimensions });
}

export function recordCount(metrics, name, value = 1) {
  if (!metrics || typeof metrics.addMetric !== 'function') throw new Error('metrics_instance_required');
  if (typeof name !== 'string' || !METRIC.test(name)) throw new Error('invalid_metric_name');
  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) throw new Error('invalid_metric_value');
  metrics.addMetric(name, MetricUnit.Count, value);
}

/** Emits an EMF JSON document to stdout; CloudWatch ingestion is asynchronous. */
export function flushMetrics(metrics) {
  if (!metrics || typeof metrics.publishStoredMetrics !== 'function') throw new Error('metrics_instance_required');
  metrics.publishStoredMetrics();
}
